clue.text: Where 26 sat summing up his assets

definitions.text: Where 26 sat summing up his assets

parts.words: Where 26 sat summing up his assets
parts.note: 26 across is the monarch of the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence, who sat in a room tallying his money

explanation.surface: A question about where a certain person did his accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is KING; the rhyme runs 'The king was in his counting-house, counting out his money', so the place where he totted up his wealth is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old office where a merchant or ruler kept accounts and counted cash is exactly the room the rhyme puts the monarch in.

clue.text: Work of poet, possibly including "Age"

indicators.note: including means one set of letters is placed inside the other
possibly says the letters of poet may be arranged in another order

parts.note: an age is an era

explanation.surface: Describing a poem that features the word Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun but the answer is the verb, as in 'machines work'. 'possibly' scrambles the poet's letters, and 'including' wraps them round the age.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, the verb sense of work.

clue.text: Animals in good shape

explanation.surface: Livestock that are fit and well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, still met in crosswords and in 'neat's-foot oil'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic term for oxen or cattle; and tidy, trim things are in good order.

clue.text: To repeat: the little Italian scoffed without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces surround this one

parts.note: IT is the short form of Italian, as in Italian vermouth
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, past tense ate
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone saying that the small Italian gobbled food without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; the surface invites reading 'without hesitation' as 'with no pause'.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, a synonym of repeat.

clue.text: They're stony, but have rent and gas to cope with

indicators.note: the letters of rent and gas must be dealt with, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Grumbling about hard-hearted people who still have bills for rent and gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stony' suggests unfeeling people, but it means made of stone: RENT and GAS rearranged give the gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnets are semi-precious gems, so they are literally stones.

clue.text: A jewel would show love, chum!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as O
a chum is a pal

explanation.surface: Giving a gem as a token of affection to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone, an example of a jewel.

clue.text: Scene made when making jelly?

explanation.surface: Wondering what scene is created while preparing a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting is the backdrop or location of a story; and jelly firms up as it sets in the fridge.

clue.text: Remember old grievances, as 9is apt to do… (4, 2, 3, 4) 9..when his digs are in primitive housing

explanation.surface: Bringing up past quarrels, just as a certain digger tends to.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 down is ARCHAEOLOGIST: literally digging up history. The held clue also carries the 9 down clue run on after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive forgotten quarrels is the idiom; an excavator of ancient sites literally turns over earlier eras.

clue.text: … when his digs are in primitive housing

definitions.text: when his digs are in primitive housing

parts.words: when his digs are in primitive housing
parts.note: digs reads as lodgings in old dwellings, but means excavations of ancient sites

explanation.surface: A man whose lodgings are in a crude old hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is British slang for rented rooms; here it means excavations at the sites of early dwellings.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of the human past excavates ancient settlements, so his digs are among prehistoric homes.

clue.text: A number bearing with ill-temper find it mean

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
E, east, is a compass bearing
rage is a fit of ill-temper

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating a bad-tempered figure and calling it unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like 'unkind' but is the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the sum divided by the count, the usual sense of average.

clue.text: Genuine high spot for an American estate agent

parts.note: genuine means real
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An authentic hilltop location being touted by a property seller.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US the word for someone who sells houses for a commission is a realtor.

clue.text: Some Icelandic women entertain in great style

indicators.note: some here means only part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Women from Iceland hosting guests lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and dash, a lively stylishness.

clue.text: Taken out, being rather old

explanation.surface: Someone escorted somewhere and feeling past their best.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dated someone is to have courted them; and something old-fashioned or passé is dated.

clue.text: Having both intelligence and aspiration

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness
aspiration in phonetics is the breathy h sound, so H

explanation.surface: Praise for someone both clever and ambitious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition, but in phonetics it is the breathed H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Accompanied by or possessing, as in 'a man with a beard', is having.

clue.text: Dress — it's an established custom

explanation.surface: A garment that has become a tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a monk's or nun's robe, or a riding outfit; it is also a settled practice.

clue.text: Given the sack, though plainly enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A sacked worker who is nonetheless eager.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dismissed from a job is to be fired; to be stirred with zeal is to be fired up.

clue.text: Senior minister making small change to report

parts.note: P, a penny, is a coin of small value
to report a story is to relate it

explanation.surface: A churchman tweaking a document slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a bishop or other high-ranking clergyman.

clue.text: Sort of roof which is peculiarly English

indicators.note: peculiarly means oddly, so the letters of English go into a strange order

explanation.surface: A roofing style found only in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle roof is covered with overlapping wooden tiles.

clue.text: A court case would appear sense

explanation.surface: A legal proceeding that seems sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial before a judge is a hearing; and listening is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Ways artillerymen used up the store of ammunition

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the whole run turns backwards

parts.note: lanes are ways or roads
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Gunners who exhausted their supply of shells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' sounds like exhausted, but in a down entry 'up' reverses LANES plus RA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a depot where weapons and munitions are kept.

clue.text: After middle-age refuse to look flashy

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
middle takes the centre letter of the word age

parts.note: refuse means rubbish, litter

explanation.surface: Advice to someone approaching fifty not to dress too loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-age' looks like a life stage; it is the centre of AGE, G. 'refuse' is the noun rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to sparkle showily, to be bright and flashy.

clue.text: New clients can get this cut out

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of clients are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Fresh customers being able to obtain a cut-out shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a sheet with a design cut out of it for painting through.

clue.text: Gardener's clock-out

parts.note: clock-out suggests ending a shift, but means a timepiece kept outdoors in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener finishing work for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A dial with a gnomon tells the time by the shadow it casts, a timepiece set out in gardens.

clue.text: The city could be elegant in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or elegant
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A town that might once have been stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large city in Illinois, USA.

clue.text: The letters column

explanation.surface: The newspaper's correspondence column.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is the mail delivered; and a post is an upright pillar.

clue.text: Sap about 50 — a writer for children

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to sap is to undermine, to mine
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A foolish fifty-year-old who writes kids' books.
explanation.walkthrough: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh. 'Sap' looks like a fool, but it is the verb meaning to tunnel under.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh stories, an example of an author of children's books.

clue.text: Head of family taking note

parts.note: kin are one's relatives, family
G is a musical note; the run of letters inside 'taking' is a coincidence, as 'taking' only joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: The head of a household paying attention to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the ruler or head of a state.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink for sale?

indicators.note: for with the question mark asks what sale could stand for when its letters are moved round

explanation.surface: Asking whether booze is being sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Access is offered in traditional fashion

indicators.note: offered in says the letters are found within the next word

explanation.surface: Entry is granted according to custom.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a mine entrance, a way of getting access underground.

clue.text: Just one T shirt or vest

parts.note: just one is single

explanation.surface: Choosing a single item of top clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless undershirt, which British speakers call a vest.

clue.text: Poles after aid in settling some foreigners

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
settling means arranging into place, so aid and in are put in a new order

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are the poles

explanation.surface: Polish people helping some immigrants settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people, but means the north and south poles. 'settling' rearranges AID IN into INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indians, people from India, are an example of foreigners from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: A brother perhaps has to finish the story

parts.note: to finish is to close
a relation is an account or story

explanation.surface: A sibling who must bring a tale to its ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling is an example of a near family member.
